newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Top Khmer Rouge commanders resign military posts.
newsitem.headline: Top Khmer Rouge commanders resign military posts.

text.p: The top two commanders of breakaway Khmer Rouge divisions in Cambodia's northwest have resigned to devote their attention to their political movement, officials said on Wednesday.

Ei Chien, commander of division 415 in Pailin, and Sok Pheap, division 450 commander in Phnom Malai, would now devote their time to the Democratic National United Movement (DNUM), an organisation started by breakaway leader Ieng Sary, an aide to Sok Pheap told Reuters.
"My commander Sok Pheap is not the divisional commander of 450 any more, as he has joined with DNUM, led by Ieng Sary," the aide to Sok Pheap said from Phnom Malai.
The aide said that Sok Pheap's deputy, Him Phon, would replace him as commander.
Em Mara, an official at the Defence Ministry, confirmed that Ei Chien had stepped down. "We are very suprised when Ei Chien told this to Second Prime Minister Hun Sen," he said.
He said Ei Chien, who has identified himself in the past as vice-chairman of DNUM, would be replaced by his deputy commander, Chhun Nhep.

Analysts of the Khmer Rouge said the move was a surprise, and that it was not yet clear whether it signalled greater political involvement for the former commanders or whether it meant they would be taking on posts in the government army.
General elections in Cambodia are set for 1998.
Ieng Sary, foreign minister during the Khmer Rouge's brutal 1975-1979 rule, broke with hardliners of the Maoist guerrilla movement in August and founded DNUM.

Ieng Sary, who was pardoned in September for his role in the genocidal regime and whose troops, believed to number up to 4,000, joined the government earlier this month, has described DNUM as a neutral movement that seeks peace with the Cambodian government.
Government officials said they did not know what Sok Pheap and Ei Chien's role in DNUM would be.

"I do not exactly understand the situation," said Nam Tum, deputy governor of Battambang province and the official charged with setting up Pailin's administrative structure. Ei Chien was divisional commander of Pailin.
"If Ei Chien had remained a divisional commander, he could have become a general in the government army," he said.
Speculation about the Khmer Rouge's future political role has been rampant in recent weeks.

Co-premiers Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Hun Sen have tried to recruit Khmer Rouge defectors to their own parties during a period of increasing tension between the coalition leaders as they begin to position themselves for the 1998 elections.

The Khmer Rouge, whose rule of terror left more than one million Cambodians dead, have been savaged by mass defections in recent months. The guerrilla group reneged on a U.N.-sponsored peace pact in 1991 and have been fighting Cambodia's coalition government.
